Isolated R1-R2 (Minor-Moderate) radio blackouts are likely on 04-05 May, with a slight chance of an R3 (Strong) event on 04-06 May. The increased radio blackout probability is primarily due to growth of Region 3296 and increased activity from Region 3293. However, a decrease to a chance of R1-R2 (Minor-Moderate) radio blackouts on 06 May is forecast due to rotation of Region 3288 beyond the limb and the more recent weakening trend of Region 3293.

No S1 (Minor) or greater solar radiation storms are expected. No significant active region activity favorable for radiation storm production is forecast.
R1 (Minor) radio blackouts are likely over 06-08 May, with a slight chance for R3 or greater events.

G1-G2 (Minor-Moderate) geomagnetic storms are likely on 07 May, G1-G3 (Minor-Strong) storms are likely on 08 May, and G1 (Minor) storms are likely on 09 May due to a combination of positive polarity CH HSS influences and the anticipated arrival of CMEs from 04 and 05 May.
No S1 (Minor) or greater solar radiation storms are expected. No significant active region activity favorable for radiation storm production is forecast.
Isolated R1-R2 (Minor-Moderate) radio blackouts are likely over 07-09 May.
G1-G3 (Minor-Strong) geomagnetic storms are likely on 08 May in response to multiple CME arrivals and positive polarity CH HSS influences. G1 (Minor) storms are likely on 09 May.
No S1 (Minor) or greater solar radiation storms are expected. No significant active region activity favorable for radiation storm production is forecast.
R1-R2 (Minor-Moderate) radio blackouts are likely over 08-10 May.

Mainly quiet to active levels are expected on 09 May, with the likelihood of an isolated, early G1 storm period still possible due to the disturbed solar wind field. A return to mainly quiet to unsettled levels is expected most of 10 May, however, CME influences later on 10 May into 11 May are likely to escalate responses to active and G1 storm levels, with a chance of isolated G2 (Moderate) storms and slight chance of G3 (Strong) levels.

The greater than 10 MeV proton flux is expected to continue at S1 levels as the solar proton event continues into 09 May. A general decline in levels is anticipated and a sub-S1 levels are likely by 10 May, with a chance that S1 levels may still be occurring. Continuing, gradual decrease in flux is expected and a return to background conditions, albeit elevated levels, are anticipated on 11 May. There is also a slight chance that S1 levels may be still be reached. There is also a risk of a re-enhancement ahead of a CME arrival later on 10 May to early 11 May.

Solar activity is likely to be moderate, with likelihood of further M-class flares (R1-R2; Minor-Moderate) and a slight chance of X-class (R3; Strong) events 09-11 May. These levels are primarily driven by the enhanced flare probabilities of Regions 3296 and 3297.

G2 (Moderate) storm levels are likely on 10 May as effects from the apparent arrival of the 7 May CME persist. Dependent upon the CME trajectory, there is a slight, and decreasing chance of G3 (Strong) levels associated with the CME effects. G1 (Minor) storms are currently anticipated on 11 May as CME influences continue; however, based on our analysis of the most recent M4 flare associated CME - this forecast may be upgraded. Currently, we anticipate active conditions on 12 May, but any CME influences from the most recent CME could continue and these levels may be upgraded accordingly as well.

The re-enhancement in the greater than 10 MeV proton flux, due to recent CME activity and 7 May CME arrival, is expected to continue through at least midday on 10 May. A decreased chance of any subsequent event exists on 11 May, decreasing to a slight chance on 12 May.

Solar activity is likely to be moderate with a continuing likelihood of M-class flares (R1-R2; Minor-Moderate) and slight chance of X-class flares (R3; Strong) 10-12 May due primarily to the enhanced flare potential of Region 3296.

Continuing CME transit will likely lead to unsettled and active levels early on 11 May, with a chance of G1 levels. Arrival of the anticipated glancing blow CME later on 11 May, will likely lead to G1-G3 (Minor to Strong) storm levels with shock arrival followed by flanking edge bulk plasma magnetic field enhancements. Any CME influences would likely lead to G1-G2 (Minor-Moderate) levels of response on 12 May, with waning effects on 13 May leading to unsettled and active responses.

The S1 event is expected to continue on 11 May, with a gradual decline anticipated to a chance of an additional or continued S1 event on 12 May and slight chance on 13 May. The current S1 storm's main contributor was likely the M4 flare on 9 May from Region 3296, which is the likely source for any additional solar proton event enhancements.

Solar activity is likely to be moderate with a continued likelihood of isolated M-class flares (R1-R2; Minor-Moderate) and a slight chance of X-class (R3; Strong) events 11-13 May primarily due to the flare probability and activity tendency of Region 3296.
